reason: Thin dark-green lines on cataphylls and petioles are lines of another colour, i.e. streaked. The colour of the lines (dark green) cannot be stated with this term.
Not a quality by itself: it modifies other verbs ('difficult to see', 'difficult to flatten'). 'Difficult to see' is already covered by inconspicuous through its own wording.
It is unclear whether the droplets are secretions, glandular dots or a drying artefact. Too few statements to give a firm reading.
Anthers or a synandrium 'forming a central porate' structure open by pores, which is poricidal.
On the stigma and pollinium, 'porate' is a pore-shaped opening or pollen aperture, not dehiscence. Too few statements to define a term; leave these unresolved.
Veins 'quilted-sunken above' lie below the surrounding blade surface, as with 'impressed' (rule C216). 'Quilted' describes the blade between the veins.
Semi-fleshy means approximately fleshy: PATO_0002351 fleshy with the approximation qualifier, as for 'sub-' words.
The firm content is that the stigma, pistil or gland bears hairs. The ring-like position cannot be stated with a term.
'Coloration variée' says only that the colour varies between plants or flowers, without naming any value. PATO_0001227 variant is relational and adds nothing.
French 'appliqué contre' means lying closely against another structure (disk against the ovary, leaf on the soil).
Claviform means club-shaped; PATO_0001883 clavate has the exact synonym club-shaped.

label: explosively dehiscent
definition: A dehiscent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's valves separating suddenly and elastically at maturity, so that the seeds are thrown out.
reason: A distinct, well-established fruit character (Oxalis, Impatiens, Euphorbiaceae). No term exists below FLOPO dehiscent.
'Égalant les étamines' compares the part's length with the stamens: an equality to another part.

A glomerule is a dense cluster of nearly sessile flowers, so these are condensed inflorescences, as with 'compact' (rule C188). PO's 'glomerule' synonym belongs to the compound capitulum and does not apply.
Stamens or fronds 'isomorphous' are all of one form, which negates dimorphic.
A compound of two shape values (linear, cuneate), handled by the continuum between two values.
'Non imbriqué' is the plain negation of the existing value imbricate.
A compound of two shape values (ovate FLOPO:0991024, reniform), handled by the continuum between two values.
French 'sillonné' means furrowed lengthwise (seed, style, midrib), which is sulcate, a child of PATO furrowed.
A synandrium is a body formed by the fusion of the stamens or anthers: like parts united, which is connate.
'Peu marqué' veins or stigma are not clearly visible, read like 'obscure' and 'indistinct' (rules C174, C175).
Aril is a part, not a quality. The colour or texture in these statements is a quality of the aril; on the seed, 'with an aril' means aril present.
Striped is an exact synonym of PATO banded. The colour of the stripes (brown) cannot be stated with this term.
A spelling variant of cauline (French 'caulinaire').
A comparison stated without its second term, like 'smaller' and 'paler' in the previous review.
Multicaule means having several stems or trunks from the base: a count of stems (at least 2) on the whole plant, not a new quality.
A compound of two shape values (ovoid, elliptic), handled by the continuum between two values.
A compound of two shape values (ovoid, fusiform), handled by the continuum between two values.

label: extrapetiolar
definition: A positional quality inhering in a stipule by virtue of the stipule's being inserted on the stem beside the base of the petiole and free from it, neither within the petiole axil nor between the petioles of opposite leaves.
reason: A standard stipule position contrasting with intrapetiolar and interpetiolar, with no PATO or FLOPO term. Sibling of FLOPO:0991074 extra-axillary.
A spelling variant of laciniate (French 'lacinié', Latin 'laciniatus').
